data.narrative:
Andrenam is a Seed-stage defense and security company founded by Matej Cernosek and Alex Chu that has raised $18M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 10 private peers and 2 public comparables in the Defense & Security sector, including UFORCE, Singularity, and NODA AI at similar or adjacent stages.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-Progression uses the $18M total raised as a proxy base value and applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement, implying a valuation of $45M. Peer-Median triangulates off three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables with a median valuation of $400M, ranging from $125M (NODA AI, Series A) to $1.0B (UFORCE, Seed). The wide dispersion reflects substantial heterogeneity in the defense-tech space at early stages.

Synthesizing both methods yields a triangulated range of $38M (low) to $460M (high), with a median of $222M. The significant gap between stage-progression and peer-median results reflects material uncertainty around Andrenam's positioning relative to the comp set. Key unknowns include the company's technical differentiation versus peers like Anduril Industries and Helsing, revenue traction or pathway to commercialization, and defensibility of its core technology. A valuation materially below the peer median would be supported by earlier technical readiness or narrower market applicability; sustained investor interest at or near the median would require evidence of superior technical capability or near-term revenue visibility.
